title: Northbridge Payroll: April 2 Pay File, 10:00 CT Cut-off

caller.name: Client Services Manager, Northbridge Payroll
caller.label: Northbridge Payroll client services, ticket NP-451377

callee.name: HR Operations Lead, Office of the CHRO
callee.label: Ironcrest CHRO office, bridged to the CMT (code 7700)

transcript.speaker: NORTHBRIDGE
transcript.text: Good morning, this is client services at Northbridge Payroll, calling on ticket N-P four five one three seven seven. I'll be direct. We have nothing from Ironcrest for the April second pay date, and our cut-off is ten o'clock Central. That's an hour from now.

transcript.speaker: NORTHBRIDGE
transcript.text: If we don't have a file by ten, about eight thousand six hundred forty people don't get paid next Friday. Your HR system feed came in at seven-twelve and again at eight-thirty-one, and both failed validation on a checksum mismatch. We can't process either one.

transcript.speaker: CHRO OFFICE
transcript.text: Understood. Our HR system is still isolated. What can you actually run for us before ten?

transcript.speaker: NORTHBRIDGE
transcript.text: Two options. One, we re-run your March nineteenth cycle exactly as it was. Same people, same hours, same amounts. Two, you send us that March nineteenth file with manual adjustments, and we load it. Either way I need a written instruction from an authorized officer on the ticket before ten.

transcript.speaker: NORTHBRIDGE
transcript.text: And one more thing. We've read the paper. Given the bank details that were leaked, do you want us to freeze all direct-deposit changes submitted since Monday? We've seen twenty-three of them. That's well above your normal week. If we freeze them, those employees get paid to the account on file before the change.

transcript.speaker: CHRO OFFICE
transcript.text: I'm putting this on the bridge for Finance and the CEO. What we can do here is manual adjustments for about one hundred forty known changes: new hires, terminations, and the overtime from the manual-mode shifts at the plants. We can have that done by nine-fifty, but only if Finance signs off. I'm emailing the same thing to the CFO now.

transcript.speaker: CHRO OFFICE
transcript.text: Treasury, a question for you as well. Is the payroll funding wire to the payroll account confirmed? The bank portal still needs single sign-on, and single sign-on is down.

transcript.speaker: NORTHBRIDGE
transcript.text: I'll hold the ticket open. I need three answers in writing before ten: which option, the officer who approves it, and freeze or no freeze on those twenty-three changes. If I don't have them by ten, the April second cycle doesn't run.

voiceStyles.NORTHBRIDGE: Woman in her 40s, calm and businesslike but firm, a busy service center behind her, speaks with clear time pressure
voiceStyles.CHRO OFFICE: Man in his 30s, tired after a night shift, quick and focused, slightly hoarse

instructorNote: Decision point: the CFO and CHRO choose and document how the pay file goes (March 19 cycle as-is, with the verified manual adjustments, or held) and what happens to the 23 direct-deposit changes. Watch whether the choice weighs unpaid employees against bank-detail fraud, whether treasury confirms the funding wire through the bank's out-of-band procedure instead of the SSO portal, whether the BCM logs payroll against its RTO, and whether the CEO approves an employee message that matches the fact sheet.
